messages.author: 6b8a5a035983f03e
messages.subject: Question about Hessian warnings
parts:
Hi,

I am running several R-INLA SPDE models with different covariates and using DIC to select the best model. When I run some of the models, I obtain a Hessian warning being less than 0, which has consequence for the accuracy of the hyperparameter.

I am able to correct the Hessian warning either by lowering the tolerance to 1e-10 or by rerunning using result = inla.rerun().

My questions are below:
1) To correct the Hessian warning, is is better to rerun using inla.rerun or is it better to lower the tolerance?

2) To compare models using DIC, do I run all of the models (regardless of whether they obtain Hessian warnings) using inla.rerun or with a lower tolerance, or do I just do these adjustments on the models that produce Hessian warnings? 

Any advice would be greatly appreciated. 

Sincerely,

Kristin

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Question about Hessian warnings
parts:
On Mon, 2021-11-15 at 15:27 -0800, KB wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I am running several R-INLA SPDE models with different covariates and
> using DIC to select the best model. When I run some of the models, I
> obtain a Hessian warning being less than 0, which has consequence for
> the accuracy of the hyperparameter.
>
> I am able to correct the Hessian warning either by lowering the
> tolerance to 1e-10 or by rerunning using result = inla.rerun().

rerun would likely fix this easier. If you run with R-4.1 a newer/st
testing version, then there is a built-in rerun as well.

you may try to add

inla(..., inla.mode="experimental")

which should also help (additional to being faster)

>
> 2) To compare models using DIC, do I run all of the models (regardless
> of whether they obtain Hessian warnings) using inla.rerun or with a
> lower tolerance, or do I just do these adjustments on the models that
> produce Hessian warnings?

I would guess DIC would be less affected by this, but generally you want
to get the Hessian right.

you may check automatically for this with

r <- inla(...)
if (sum(abs(r$misc$cov.intern[upper.tri(r$misc$cov.intern)])) == 0) {
r <- inla.rerun(r)
}


--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org
